verdicts.reason: Quote directly states testbench/reference model must be built independently of generated RTL. It is a process requirement with nothing to check in simulation, so check=none is right.
Quote states the RTL must not define expected results. It is a process constraint, so check=none and MUST_NOT are right.

TEST-001 states the expected result that the independent model matches addresses, data and responses for FIXED/INCR/WRAP with legal sizes. This is checked by a directed or random scenario against the model.
TEST-003 gives the expected result of stable payload through APB wait and RREADY/BREADY stalls, with test type Assertions. Stability is checkable every cycle from interface signals.

duplicates.reason: Both come from the same sentence about keeping the testbench independent of the RTL. However, AB-15.1-01 says the testbench is built independently, while AB-15.1-02 says the RTL must not define expected results. The strength and subject differ, so they are not true duplicates. Merging is not recommended.

questions.question: TEST-003 does not say which payload signals must stay stable during stalls (for example AWADDR, WDATA, PADDR, PWDATA, RDATA, RRESP), or the exact stall conditions. Define the signal set and the stall conditions.
TEST-001 does not define 'legal sizes' (for example the maximum size against the data width), nor the burst lengths and alignment. Define them so that stimulus and expected results can be written.
